title: Nested if in the else branch
idea: A nested if can live inside the else, not just the if. This is one way to express 'otherwise, ask another question' - and shows why elif often reads better. Predict output.

exercises.prompt: Where can a nested if be placed?
options: Inside the if branch, the else branch, or both
Only at the very top of the file
exercises.explanation: Any branch is just a body of code, so an if can be nested inside the if branch, the else branch, or both.
55 >= 90 is False, so we enter the else. Inside, 55 >= 50 is True, so 'Pass'.
40 >= 90 False, into the else; 40 >= 50 False, so the inner else: 'Fail'.

exercises.prompt: This 'if inside else' pattern does the same job as which flatter structure?
exercises.explanation: 'else: if ...' is exactly what elif is short for. 'if A / elif B / else' reads more cleanly than nesting an if in the else.

exercises.prompt: 'else:' then an indented 'if' on the next line behaves like an 'elif'.
exercises.explanation: Yes - elif is literally shorthand for an if nested in an else. Both check the second condition only when the first was False.

exercises.prompt: Rewrite the nested-in-else grade code as a flat elif chain (arrange the lines).
exercises.explanation: The elif chain is the flat, readable version of 'if A / else: if B / else'. Same outcomes, less indentation.

exercises.prompt: When is a REAL nested if (not just elif) the right tool?
options: When the inner question depends on being inside a branch, e.g. only ask about seats after confirming a ticket
Only when the conditions are numbers
exercises.explanation: elif chains pick one bucket from a flat list. Real nesting is for a second question that only makes sense inside a particular branch.
member is False, so we enter the else; age 70 >= 65 is True, so 'Senior discount'.

exercises.prompt:
Collapse 'else: if age >= 65:' into one keyword:

if member:
    print("Free")
____ age >= 65:
    print("Senior discount")
else:
    print("Full price")
exercises.explanation: elif replaces the 'else:' plus nested 'if'. The result is the same but flatter and easier to read.

options: It works, but an elif chain usually reads better for picking one of several buckets
It changes the output compared to elif
exercises.explanation: Nesting in the else is valid, but elif is the clean idiom for a flat list of buckets. Save true nesting for dependent questions.
